{{ElectionsOH}}
The '''2018 Ohio State Auditor election''' was held on November 6, 2018, to elect the [[Ohio State Auditor]], concurrently with an election to the [[2018 United States Senate election in Ohio|U.S. Senate]], [[2018 Ohio gubernatorial election|governor]], [[2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Ohio|U.S. House of Representatives]], and other [[2018 Ohio elections|state]] and [[2018 United States elections#Local elections|local]] elections. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] auditor [[Dave Yost]] was term-limited and could not seek re-election to a third consecutive term. Primary elections were held on May 8, 2018, though both the Republican and Democratic nominees ran uncontested.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schultze |first=M.L. |date=March 6, 2018 |title=Auditor Candidate Zack Space Talks About the Failure of ECOT Oversight |url=https://www.ideastream.org/news/government-politics/2018-03-06/auditor-candidate-zack-space-talks-about-the-failure-of-ecot-oversight |access-date=September 14, 2025 |website=Ideastream Public Media}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=2018 Ohio Primary Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2018/05/08/us/elections/results-ohio-primary-elections.html |access-date=September 14, 2025 |website=The New York Times |date=8 May 2018 }}</ref> A debate was held on October 19, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harris |first=Nate |date=October 19, 2018 |title=State Auditor race: Faber, Space duke it out at Zane State debate |url=https://www.zanesvilletimesrecorder.com/story/news/2018/10/19/faber-space-duke-out-zane-state-debate/1695053002/ |url-access=limited |access-date=September 14, 2025 |website=Zanesville Times Recorder}}</ref>

[[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] state representative and former state senator [[Keith Faber]] defeated former [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] U.S. representative [[Zack Space]] in the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 6, 2018 |title=GOP state Rep. Keith Faber elected as Ohio auditor |url=https://myfox28columbus.com/news/local/gop-state-rep-keith-faber-elected-as-ohio-auditor |access-date=September 14, 2025 |website=FOX 28 |publisher=Associated Press}}</ref> Both major party candidates were accused of serious legal issues and mismanagement of state funds during the campaign, with Faber being attacked due to the federal investigation of [[Cliff Rosenberger]] and the [[Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow|ECOT]] scandal, and Space due to late tax payments and a [[law license]] suspension.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ellerbock |first=Josh |date=October 19, 2018 |title=Faber, Space duke it out for auditor |url=https://www.sidneydailynews.com/2018/10/19/faber-space-duke-it-out-for-auditor/ |access-date=September 14, 2025 |website=Sidney Daily News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 19, 2018 |title=Auditor Candidates Trade Barbs on Late Tax Payments |url=https://www.ideastream.org/news/government-politics/2018-10-19/auditor-candidates-trade-barbs-on-late-tax-payments |access-date=September 14, 2025 |website=Ideastream Public Media |language=en}}</ref>

== Republican primary ==
=== Candidates ===
==== Nominee ====
* [[Keith Faber]], [[List of presidents of the Ohio Senate|President of the Ohio Senate]] (2013-2016), state senator from the 12th district (2007-2016), and state representative from the 84th district (2001-2007, 2017-2019)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dispatch.com/news/20170131/keith-faber-confirms-run-for-state-auditor|title=Keith Faber confirms run for state auditor|work=The Columbus Dispatch|last=Ludlow|first=Randy|date=January 31, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2017}}</ref>

====Declined====
* [[Cliff Rosenberger]], Speaker of the Ohio House of Representatives<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2017/10/ohio_house_speaker_cliff_rosen_1.html|title=Ohio House Speaker Cliff Rosenberger mulls run for state auditor|work=The Plain Dealer|last=Pelzer|first=Jeremy|date=October 24, 2017|access-date=October 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2017/10/house_speaker_cliff_rosenberge_1.html|title=House Speaker Cliff Rosenberger says he won't run for state auditor|work=The Plain Dealer|last=Kilpatrick|first=Mary|date=October 30, 2017|access-date=November 5, 2017}}</ref>
